title: Nine Governor Races Make History Across the Country
summary:
Voters in nine states made history on Tuesday with their choices for governor, electing a string of firsts across the country.

In Georgia, Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms will become the country's first Black woman elected governor of any state. The former Atlanta mayor, who served as an adviser to former President Joe Biden, defeated Republican Rick Jackson and became the first Democrat to win a Georgia governor's race in more than two decades.

In New Mexico, Democrat Deb Haaland, who is of Pueblo Indian descent, will be the first Native American woman governor in U.S. history. Haaland, who defeated Republican Gregg Hull, had already made history as one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and as the first Native American Cabinet secretary.

California and Texas also elected Latino firsts. Democrat Xavier Becerra will be California's first elected Latino governor, succeeding Governor Gavin Newsom after defeating Republican Steve Hilton. Democrat Gina Hinojosa will be Texas's first Latina governor, defeating incumbent Republican Governor Greg Abbott and becoming the state's first Democratic governor in more than 30 years.

Florida and Wisconsin elected their first Black governors: Republican Byron Donalds in Florida, who beat Democrat David Jolly, and Democrat David Crowley in Wisconsin, who beat Republican Congressman Tom Tiffany.

Three more women made history. Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn became the first woman to win a governor's race in Tennessee. Democrat Amy Klobuchar will become Minnesota's first woman governor. And in one of the night's bigger upsets, Democrat Amy Acton is set to become Ohio's first woman elected governor and the state's first Jewish governor, defeating Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.

From coast to coast, Tuesday's governor races redrew the map of who can hold a state's top job.
why_it_matters: Governors run state schools, roads and services, and these firsts widen the picture of who can hold a state's top job.

background_read: A governor leads a U.S. state, a bit like a president leads the whole country, running state services and signing state laws.
Governors are chosen in state elections, and many states had never before elected a woman, a Black leader or a Latino leader to the job.
Each governor's race is decided by voters in that state alone, which is why every state's 'first' is its own separate piece of history.
